sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The original states that this subspecies is best identified by mitochondrial genome sequences; soldiers and workers cannot be distinguished from the other three subspecies. The alate is close to the Malawi subspecies (I. u. malawii, but the two do not overlap in distribution), on average the largest of the four subspecies with the longest wings: IWgL = 18.9—19.5 mm, versus 13.6—18.1 mm in the other two subspecies (no measurements yet available for malawii). Alate measurements (Table 17, n=3): IEyD 0.41—0.45 mm, IHdW 1.72—1.84 mm, IMlAmD 0.20—0.23 mm, IOcD 0.15—0.18 mm, IPcW 0.85—0.93 mm, IPnW 1.61—1.74 mm, IT3L 2.07—2.20 mm, IMlAmD/IMlmmD = 0.93—1.20, IEyD/IHdW = 0.23—0.25.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Coloration, setae and structure essentially as in the species-level description of I. ugandensis (head capsule C6—C8, frontal gland pore nearly concolorous with the head capsule, pronotum C5—C7, wings transparent with a brown-grey tinge, tergites C6—C7; head capsule with a dense felt of short fine hairs and conspicuous setae, fore coxa with 7—12 strong setae on the ridge, tibiae with 15—30 spines and tibial spur formula 3/2/2; compound eyes oval, ocelli short to medium-oval, antennae 16-segmented, labrum domed, left mandible apical tooth medium to small and more prominent than the first marginal tooth, 3 marginal teeth, right mandible with 2 marginal teeth, pronotum flat to very weakly saddle-shaped, fore coxa ridged, wings with R1 fused to the margin, Rs single, M with 2—5 and Cu with 9—12 branches). Alate measurements of this subspecies (Table 17, n=3): IEyD 0.41—0.45 mm, IHdW 1.72—1.84 mm, IOcD 0.15—0.18 mm, IPnW 1.61—1.74 mm, IWgL 18.9—19.5 mm, IEyD/IHdW = 0.23—0.25. The alate of this subspecies is distinctly the largest of the four subspecies (ugke in the PCA), with the longest wings on average: IWgL = 18.9—19.5 mm, versus 13.6—18.1 mm in the other two subspecies (no measurements available yet for malawii).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The original does not describe the soldier of this subspecies separately; the morphology is that of the species-level description of I. ugandensis: head capsule generally distinctly inflated, left mandible slightly curved to nearly straight and distinctly less curved than the right (SMlc/SMrc = 0.68—1.02), head length SHdL 2.73—3.72 mm, head width SHdW 1.86—2.37 mm, left mandible ventral length SMlL 2.15—2.74 mm, mandible minor curvature SMlc 0.12—0.27 mm (measurements for the whole species, Table 16); soldiers cannot be distinguished among the four subspecies.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The original does not describe the worker of this subspecies separately; the morphology is that of the species-level description of I. ugandensis: enteric valve of the fungifaber type (about 6% of specimens intermediate between fungifaber and finitimus), the enteric valve on average slightly larger than in I. minitabundus, the odd primary cushion about 16% longer than the even ones, the crest generally absent or very weak; head width WHdW 1.11—1.42 mm, mean length of enteric valve primary cushions 0.62—0.85 mm, width 0.06—0.12 mm, mean length of secondary cushions 0.55—0.73 mm, width 0.30—0.45 mm, odd primary cushion elongation index 5.57—12.1 (measurements for the whole species, Table 16); workers cannot be distinguished among the four subspecies.

note: Adapted from the genus revision in Josens et al. (2025), original in English; the original treats this taxon as a subspecies (I. ugandensis is divided into four subspecies on alate body size and compound eye and ocellus dimensions, molecular data still scarce); the original does not describe the soldier and worker of each subspecies separately but refers to the species-level description; measurements from Table 17 and the text of the original; distribution, hosts, DNA and figure numbers are not translated.
